newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Kazakh authorities arrest Chinese Uighurs -exiles.
newsitem.headline: Kazakh authorities arrest Chinese Uighurs -exiles.

text.p: Exiles from China's Moslem Uighur community said on Monday that Kazakh authorities had last week arrested three ethnic Uighurs who had fled to Kazakhstan from the turbulent northwest Chinese province of Xinjiang.

"According to our information, the Kazakh authorities plan to hand these people over to China," Mukhiddin Mukhlisi, spokesman for the separatist United National Revolutionary Front of East Turkestan, told Reuters in the Kazakh capital Almaty.
Interior ministry and legal officials in the former Soviet republic said they had no information about the arrests.

But Mukhlisi said 27-year old Gappar Ablimit was arrested as he was working in a local market at the end of last month. He said Akhmed Khelim, 25, and another Uighur man named only as Azat were arrested on Saturday.
Mukhlisi said the three, who left Xinjiang last year, were arrested in connection with a Uighur demonstration outside the Chinese embassy in Almaty last month.
"The arrests are bad. Hopes that our cause will be understood here are fading," Mukhlisi said.
Exile groups in Almaty say they have considered moving their organisations from Kazakhstan to Turkey or to Germany.
Uighur exile groups protested against China following bloody anti-Chinese riots in Xinjiang in February. The Kazakh government has made only guarded comment on the Xinjiang riots.

Security Council chief Beksultan Sarsekov voiced concern last month over instability caused by Uighur unrest. He called on the Chinese authorities for restraint in dealing with the Uighurs, who share with the Kazakhs a Turkic language and Islam.
But Kazakhstan and other ex-Soviet Central Asian states are sensitive to pressure from China, with whom they and Russia plan to to sign a pact later this month reducing frontier garrisons.
